newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts up on short cover.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts up on short cover.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Thursday in a sluggish session, with short covering after recent losses lifting the front of the complex despite a softer physical market, industry sources said.
July edged up 0.9 cent to close at $2.08 per million British thermal units. August settled 0.1 cent lower at $2.106. Others ended on either side of unchanged.

"We saw a little short covering late in the day and we're getting more on ACCESS. Certainly, the market was oversold, but I think the technical picture looks pretty negative," said one Texas-based trader.

While chartists agreed the market was oversold and due for a bounce after a five percent slide in three sessions, most agreed July's close Wednesday below $2.08 turned the technical picture decidedly bearish. They expected a test of psychological support at $2 and possibly a break to the mid-$1.90s. July resistance was seen at $2.155, $2.21, $2.25, $2.37 and the contract high of $2.44.
"Unless July gets back above $2.15, I'm bearish," the Texas trader said.
Sources said revised forecasts for above-normal weather across southern tier states next week may have triggered some buying. Northern states mostly are expected to stay seasonal.

In the cash Thursday, swing gas at the Louisiana Gulf was talked a couple of cents lower in the low-teens. Midcon pipes lost a few cents to the high-$1.90s-2.00. New York city gate gas lost similar ground to the high-$2.30s-2.40.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip was unchanged at $2.196. NYMEX said 33,083 contracts traded, down slightly from Wednesday's revised tally of 35,006.

On the KCBT, July finished 0.2 cent higher at $1.95, while deferreds ended steady to up one cent. The East/West spread widened by 0.7 cent to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 198 lots traded, down from Wednesday's total of 338.
